mechanism: scripts/affordance_audit.py computes an affordance's use rate as uses/denominator and treats a low rate as a finding (AVAILABLE-NOT-ADVERTISED or ADVERTISED-UNUSED). When the corpus contains zero played actions the denominator is zero, the rate is coerced to 0.0, and every gameplay-dependent affordance is reported as unused. But on a corpus with no gameplay an empty `transitions` is CORRECTLY not queried, so the zero is the absence of a measurement, not the presence of a behaviour.
summary: Run against the local trace store the audit emitted 14 confident findings -- all six game actions plus transitions, history, animation, previous_frame, last_transition, last_action, last_action_frame, latest_frame -- from a store of 211 calls in which game_id and action_num are NULL for every row and 0 actions were played. It is last night's latency screens, not gameplay. Added a GAMEPLAY_DEPENDENT set and an UNMEASURED-NO-GAMEPLAY verdict; the tool now suppresses 16 non-findings on that corpus while the real findings on a genuine 2,971-action gameplay pull (RESET and ACTION5, AVAILABLE-NOT-ADVERTISED) survive unchanged, which is the negative control on the guard itself. Consequence beyond the tool: the campaign's standing root cause -- that the agent never queries `transitions` -- is currently UNMEASURABLE on both instruments we own, because a Kaggle pull keeps only a last-call prose snapshot and the local store has no games.
lesson: A rate with a zero denominator is not a low rate, it is no measurement, and a tool that coerces it to 0.0 will manufacture its own headline finding on the day it is pointed at the wrong corpus. Guard the denominator, not just the numerator. Corollary, and the more expensive one: a root cause the campaign has treated as established for weeks turned out to have no instrument that can currently measure it -- before building a repair for an affordance-use failure, confirm the corpus can see use at all.
